pick_hub.title: ELRO Connects hubs found
pick_hub.description: These K2 hubs answered on your network. Pick the one to add, or choose manual entry to type the details in yourself - which is also how a K1 hub is set up, since a K1 does not answer the discovery broadcast.

data_description.selected_hub: Each entry shows the hub's Device ID and the address it answered from. No further details are needed: a hub that answers this broadcast is a K2, and Control Key and App ID apply to K1 hubs only.

manual.title: ELRO Connects Real-time Hub Setup
manual.description: Enter your ELRO Connects hub connection details. A K1 hub always has to be set up this way; a K2 hub only when the network scan did not find it. You can find the Device ID in your ELRO Connects app or hub settings.

data_description.host: The IP address of your ELRO Connects hub on your local network
data_description.device_id: The unique device identifier of your ELRO Connects hub, usually starts with 'ST_'
data_description.ctrl_key: Control key for authentication (leave default unless specified)
data_description.app_id: Application ID for authentication (leave default unless specified)
data_description.protocol: Leave on 'auto' to probe the hub. K1 speaks plain JSON, K2 (SF50GA) speaks the XOR-framed protocol handled by the elro-connects-k2-protocol library.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the ELRO Connects hub. Please verify the IP address and ensure the hub is powered on and connected to your network.

abort.already_configured: This ELRO Connects hub is already configured.

init.title: ELRO Connects Real-time Options
init.description: Debug logging writes every UDP frame exchanged with the hub to the Home Assistant log, for this integration and for the K2 protocol library. Leave it off for normal use.

data_description.debug_logging: Takes effect immediately, no restart or reload needed. The log can be downloaded from Settings > System > Logs.

hub_silent.title: ELRO Connects hub {device_id} is not answering
hub_silent.description:
Home Assistant has not received a single reply from the ELRO Connects hub at **{host}** (`{device_id}`), so no devices could be created.

Diagnosis: {details}

What to check:

1. **The hub's own internet access.** A K2 hub appears to stop answering even local requests when it cannot reach the ELRO cloud, which is hosted in China. One user traced exactly these symptoms to a firewall rule that blocked Chinese address space; removing it fixed the integration. This has not been confirmed independently, but if you geo-block or otherwise restrict outbound traffic, allow the hub out and reload the integration.
2. **UDP port 1025**, open in both directions and free on the Home Assistant host. Nothing else may hold it - not a second copy of this integration, and not `elro_test_tool.py` running on the same machine.
3. **A direct path to the hub.** In a container, Home Assistant needs host networking: on its own bridge network the hub's replies never come back.
4. **The IP address and Device ID**, and that the hub is powered on and on the same network.

Enable *debug logging* in the integration options to log every UDP frame exchanged with the hub. This notification disappears on its own once the hub reports a device.

hub_not_armed.title: ELRO Connects hub {device_id} is ignoring Home Assistant
hub_not_armed.description:
The ELRO Connects hub at **{host}** is sending Home Assistant frames, but it has never acknowledged an activation ping, so it is ignoring every command sent to it and no devices could be created.

Diagnosis: {details}

What to check:

1. **The Device ID.** The hub only arms a session for a request that names it exactly; `{device_id}` must match the ID printed on the hub / shown in the ELRO Connects app, character for character (including the `ST_` prefix and its case). A mismatch produces exactly this: frames arrive, commands are dropped in silence.
2. **UDP port 1025 must be free on the Home Assistant host.** If another process holds it, the hub's replies can be delivered to that process instead of to Home Assistant.
3. **The hub's own internet access.** A K2 hub appears to go quiet when it cannot reach the ELRO cloud, which is hosted in China. One user traced a hub that reported nothing to a firewall rule that blocked Chinese address space; removing it fixed the integration. This has not been confirmed independently, but if you geo-block or otherwise restrict outbound traffic, allow the hub out and reload the integration.

Enable *debug logging* in the integration options to log every UDP frame exchanged with the hub. This notification disappears on its own once the hub reports a device.

hub_no_devices.title: ELRO Connects hub {device_id} reports no devices
hub_no_devices.description:
The ELRO Connects hub at **{host}** (`{device_id}`) is answering Home Assistant, but it reports no devices, so no entities could be created.

Diagnosis: {details}

What to check:

1. **Are the detectors paired with this hub?** Confirm in the ELRO Connects app that they show up there, then call the `elro_connects_realtime.sync_devices` action to ask again.
2. **The hub's own internet access.** A K2 hub appears to serve its device list only while it can reach the ELRO cloud, which is hosted in China. One user traced exactly these symptoms to a firewall rule that blocked Chinese address space; removing it fixed the integration. This has not been confirmed independently, but if you geo-block or otherwise restrict outbound traffic, allow the hub out and reload the integration.
3. **Battery and range** of the detectors: a sub-device the hub has lost contact with is left out of the list.

Enable *debug logging* in the integration options to log every UDP frame exchanged with the hub. This notification disappears on its own once the hub reports a device.
